doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Never touring Europe and preferring the quartet
summary: He turned down European tours with big bands, has only been to South America with Krupa, and now prefers the quartet.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you have the chance to travel overseas?

No, I always turned it down. I didn’t want to go with the big bands. I didn’t want to be — see I’m a small group player. If I had an opportunity, like with South America, I went with Gene Krupa with the small group, that was different. But with big bands you’re © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

squashed, your subdued, you can’t really open up and blow. And I was really never happy with that. I’ve done it, but I turned down Woody, Thad, anybody Benny, they all went to Europe, I’m probably the only jazz artist that hasn’t been to Europe. But I’ve been to South America with Gene Krupa.
Well after a time in the big bands it must have been a real pleasure to find yourself back with the quartet and do what you were doing.
Yeah. That’s what I’ve been doing recently.
